description: Rule-sensitive positions for legality diagnostics. Declared characteristics are verified against exact chess logic at load, so a mislabeled position fails instead of silently weakening the suite. Positions may hold properties they do not declare; declaring one that is absent is the error.

positions.notes: Back-rank check with exactly one legal reply, so masking cannot hide a wrong distribution.
The same pattern with the escape square blocked by its own pawn.
Not in check and no legal move, so terminal handling cannot rely on check alone.
Ruy Lopez with the d-pawn advanced, so the c6 knight is absolutely pinned against the king.
Both sides retain full rights and White can castle on either wing immediately.
Rights are present on both wings but own pieces block every castle, separating rights from availability.
White may capture en passant on f6.
The FEN advertises an en passant target square that no pawn can actually capture on.
A single pawn promotes, so every promotion piece must be a distinct action.
Promotion is available by advance and by capture, doubling the promotion actions.
A sparse king-and-pawn endgame in the smallest legal-move-count bucket.
An open middlegame with a wide branching factor in the largest bucket.
